newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MARCH 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MARCH 26.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Dramatic developments from Ankara as the Turkish chief of staff says he is opening a "door to dialogue" with his surprise appearance at a Greek embassy reception for yesterday's independence day celebrations. Yesterday marked the first time that Turkish airplanes did not infringe Aegean airspace. Athens' response: impressive words but actions speak louder.
--Following his impressive win at the conservative opposition New Democracy congress on Friday, Costas Karamanlis is now seeking his shadow cabinet from all the party's tendencies.
--Albanian's Prime Minister Bashkim Fino says that he will support institutions, in his efforts to bring calm back to Albania.

--As the deadline for tax declaration submissions approaches, tax officials are calling for an extension to the deadline, saying the bulk of declarations have yet to be seen and, of those submitted, seven in ten have serious mistakes.
--Albanian PM Fino is expected to visit Athens in the next few weeks for talks.

--New Democracy's new leader has led the opposition party to a five-point lead over ruling party PASOK in the latest opinion polls. According to the results, Karamanlis leads Prime Minister Costas Simitis in popularity by another five points.
--The death of a 21-year-old after taking antibiotics has brought the issue of unmonitored dispensing of antibiotics and the dangers of allergic reactions to the fore.
--Attractive loan financing for new car purcahses has boosted trade at major car dealerships. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
